\section{Discussion}
Conservation fixes the accessible equilibrium temperature, while the contact law sets the relaxation rate. The two heat capacities enter that rate because both temperatures respond to the same exchanged heat. This explains the factor of two for equal capacities and its absence when one body remains at a fixed bath temperature.

The constant heat capacities and conductance restrict the time dependence established here: temperature-dependent parameters need not give the same exponential law. Internal equilibrium within each body is a separate restriction; spatial gradients can invalidate a description by only two temperatures. The calculation contains no experimental measurements and identifies no microscopic transport mechanism, so exact solvability supplies neither experimental accuracy nor a microscopic explanation.
